Research indicates that poisoning-based backdoors in neural networks cannot be installed with the same asymmetry seen in cryptographic systems, which would prevent defenders from learning about them. Instead, such backdoors are reconstructible by defenders with adequate observational data, challenging the notion that these attacks can remain hidden. Experimental validation on large language models corroborates the findings, showing that effective backdoors are not impervious to defenders.

 - Poisoning-based backdoor attacks in neural networks do not exhibit the same security characteristics as cryptographic systems.
 - Defenders can learn and reconstruct backdoor verifiers using data from observed triggers.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28045

A new approach in reinforcement learning has been proposed to address the issue of outcome-level mode collapse, which occurs when algorithms focus on a smaller subset of potential outcomes despite multiple comparable options being available. The method, known as inverse probability scaling, aims to change learning dynamics to ensure a more diverse exploration of high-quality outcomes, improving performance across various tasks.

 - Expected return maximization in reinforcement learning can lead to mode collapse, limiting outcome diversity.
 - Inverse probability scaling offers a solution by changing the learning dynamics to prevent this collapse.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21669
